newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices firm again, helped by crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices firm again, helped by crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices continued to gain ground Thursday in lackluster trade, still buoyed by a stable crude market and some East Coast utility interest, industry sources said.

"There has been some demand from utilities and we had a big move (up). Now it depends on crude and weather," said one East Coast trader, noting eastern utility loads have been light due to mild weather.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent climbed 40 cents to about the $16 a barrel level on reports a cargo for May 25-June 10 delivery sold at $16.25.
A traders said June paper sold at $16.60, up 25 cents on the day, but the deal was not confirmed. NYH July one percent paper was bid in the $16.60 area, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour was 35 cents higher at $16.50-75.
New York high sulphurs notionally were up a quarter, with 2.2 percent now pegged around $14.75.
U.S. Gulf three percent edged up slightly to $14.50, while one percent held steady in the high-$14s.

New York city gate swing gas prices edged up a couple of cents Wednesday to the high-$2.40s/mmBtu, or about $15.62 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, gained slightly to the mid-$2.20s/mmBtu, or $14.18 a barrel.
